expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: "Your situation—users *keep* accidentally deleting workspaces—is exactly where a modal *fails*"

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: "Users trained by dozens of benign 'OK' clicks will dismiss 'Are you sure?' reflexively"

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: Listed #1: "Soft-delete + trash (rung 1 — control). When a user deletes a workspace, move it to trash...Keep it for 30 days"

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
expectations.evidence: Listed #2: "Grace-period undo (rung 2 — warning). Delete immediately, but show 'Workspace deleted. [Undo]' as a toast"

expectations.text: Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
expectations.evidence: Listed #3: "Type-to-confirm...require the user to type the workspace name to confirm deletion"

expectations.text: If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: No explicit dialog option that shows both workspace name and scale of data loss

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
expectations.evidence: Clear 1-2-3 numbered ranking with rung designations
